Star Wars is one of the most well-known multimedia franchises in the world. George Lucas created the epic space opera. Lucas is considered one of the most significant figures of the 20th-century New Hollywood movement and a pioneer of the modern blockbuster. His film career might never have happened if it weren’t for the horrible accident he was in a few days before he graduated high school. Growing up, Lucas wanted to be a racecar driver. He was a regular on the underground racing circuit. On June 12, 1962, while driving a souped-up Autobianchi Bianchina, he was in a terrible car accident. He was t-boned, and his car flipped multiple times. His seat belt snapped, and he was ejected from the car, which saved his life. After the accident, Lucas lost his enthusiasm for racing cars and pursued other interests, including filmmaking.

Before he created Star Wars, George Lucas made a film called American Graffiti in 1973. Despite its low budget, it earned over $50 million at the box office and several award nominations. His early success inspired him to continue as a writer and director. He and his partner Gary Kurtz were very excited about a project they had been working on since 1971. The story was based on outer space adventures. There were plenty of sci-fi films at the time, but most were dark dystopian tales. Lucas wanted to make a different kind of sci-fi film. In an interview, he said, “I want to give young people some sort of faraway exotic environment for their imaginations to run around in.” Lucas and Kurtz took their 12-page film treatment to studios in Hollywood, such as United Artists and Universal, but got turned down. The situation looked grim until 20th Century Fox decided to invest in the project.

Early drafts of the Star Wars films would be unrecognizable to fans today. It took years for George Lucas to refine his script. His friend and mentor, Francis Ford Coppola, expressed misgivings about early drafts. In the first draft, Luke Skywalker was a grizzled old general instead of a farm boy turned Jedi. The dark side of the force was called “The Bogan,” and Han Solo was an amphibian-like alien. The second draft introduced the menacing Darth Vader, and in the third draft, Obi-Wan Kenobi appeared. Lucas struggled to write dialogue and enlisted the assistance of other writers and his team of directors. The fourth draft was completed on January 1, 1976, and used when production began in Tunisia on March 25, 1976. Lucas chose Tunisia for its other-worldly desert landscapes and unique structures. Mark Hamill, who played Luke Skywalker, said that the desert in Tunisia felt just as remote as the fictional world it portrayed.

Many scenes from early drafts of Star Wars were altered or eliminated completely because they would have been prohibitively expensive to shoot. George Lucas and Gary Kurtz originally budgeted $18 million for the first film, Star Wars Episode IV: A New Hope. 20th Century Fox offered them $7.5 million, and they took the offer. The franchise’s first film was released in 1977 and ushered in a new era of movie-making. Star Wars fundamentally changed the aesthetics and narratives of Hollywood films. Before Star Wars, special effects in films had not appreciably advanced since the 1950s. The commercial success of Star Wars created a boom in state-of-the-art special effects in the late 1970s. One factor in the film's success was its use of the monomyth, or “hero's journey,” template. Although the final budget was $11 million, the film grossed more than $513 million worldwide during its initial release.
